summary: A use-after-free bug reads or writes memory through a pointer after that memory has been released. The pointer is dangling: it still holds the old address, but the storage may now belong to something else.

sections.heading: How a pointer dangles
bullets: Heap block freed while another pointer still references it.
A function returns the address of a local variable.
A pointer outlives the block-scoped variable it points to.

sections.heading: Heap example
Stack examples
Why it is dangerous
sections.body: The allocator may hand the freed block to a new allocation, so the stale pointer now aliases unrelated data. Attackers exploit this by getting a controlled object placed in the freed slot, turning a dangling write into corruption or code execution.

sections.heading: How to avoid it
bullets: Set pointers to NULL immediately after `free`.
Never return the address of a local; use `static`, heap memory, or an out-parameter.
Give each allocation a single clear owner responsible for freeing.
Test with AddressSanitizer, which poisons freed memory and reports the access.

sections.body: A second `free` on the same pointer corrupts allocator bookkeeping and is exploitable. Nulling after free turns it into the harmless `free(NULL)`.

subtopics.title: Wild, dangling, null, void recap
subtopics.summary: Four pointer states to tell apart.

bullets: void*: generic type, not a state.

sections.body: Document who owns each pointer. Prefer APIs where the callee takes ownership or the caller keeps it, never both. Reference counting or arenas (free everything at once) reduce per-object lifetime errors.

subtopics.title: Detecting with ASan and Valgrind
subtopics.summary: See the bug, not just the crash.

sections.body: Compile with `-fsanitize=address -g` and run; the report shows the free site, the bad access, and the allocation site. Valgrind's memcheck gives similar traces without recompiling.

takeaways: A dangling pointer outlives its target; using it is undefined behavior.
Null pointers after free; never return addresses of locals.
Freed memory can be reused, so bugs can be silent and exploitable.
Use sanitizers to catch these early.
